Alright, I've set up the project directory with the HTML scaffold, the main three.js script, and a Playwright capture script to take screenshots at key beats. The next logical step is to actually execute that capture script so I can see the rendered film and verify that everything works as intended.

First, I should ensure that Playwright is installed and available in the project. I already ran a check earlier (`npx -y playwright --version`) which confirmed that Playwright version 1.55.1 is present, so the dependency is satisfied. The capture script (`capture.mjs`) imports `chromium` from Playwright and launches Edge in headless mode, navigates to the local server, clicks the play button, and then takes screenshots at predefined timestamps. All that code is now written to disk.

Before I run the script, I need to make sure I'm in the correct working directory so that Node can resolve the relative imports and find the `node_modules` folder where Playwright resides. The project lives at `C:\Users\aranr\claude-projects\3d-modeling-and-animations\wind-up-chase`. Changing to that directory will also ensure that the local HTTP server I started earlier (serving on port 8741) is still running and serving the `index.html` that references `main.js`.

I also want to verify that the `npm ls playwright` command runs without error, confirming that Playwright is indeed listed as a dependency. Even if it isn’t listed explicitly, the earlier version check showed the binary is available, but a quick `npm ls` will give me a clean confirmation and also avoid any hidden issues.

Now, to actually execute the capture script, I’ll run `node capture.mjs`. This will launch the headless Edge browser, load the three.js scene, start the animation, and produce the dailies screenshots. Since the film is 60 seconds long, I should allow enough timeout for the whole process; 180 seconds (3 minutes) should be ample.

Putting it all together, the PowerShell command I need is:

1. `cd` into the project folder.
2. Run `npm ls playwright` to confirm the dependency (redirect errors to null to keep output clean).
3. Execute `node capture.mjs` to perform the capture.

Thus, the exact command string I’ll pass to the PowerShell tool is:

`cd C:\Users\aranr\claude-projects\3d-modeling-and-animations\wind-up-chase; npm ls playwright 2>$null; node capture.mjs`

I'll also set a timeout of 180000 ms to ensure the script has enough time to finish. This will give me the dailies I need to review the cinematography and decide if any adjustments are required.
